 Advertisement NWS lets first tornado warning expire for Santa Cruz County; second remains
 Advertisement Updated: 1:05 PM PST Nov 16, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Ricardo Tovar Digital Content Manager NWS lets first tornado warning expire for Santa Cruz County; second remains
 Updated: 1:05 PM PST Nov 16, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Ricardo Tovar Digital Content Manager BOULDER CREEK, Calif. — The National Weather Service issued a second tornado warning Monday for part of Santa Cruz County, with the new warning set to expire at 1:30 p.m.
 Advertisement The National Weather Service allowed a tornado warning for west-central Santa Cruz County to expire at 1 p.m. Monday after the storm weakened below severe limits. 
 The NWS said the storm no longer appeared capable of producing a tornado, but gusty winds and heavy rain remained possible.
 A second tornado warning, covering an area near Davenport and Bonny Doon, is set to expire at 1:30 p.m. The NWS map estimated 1,284 people and one school were in that warning area; no hospitals were included.
 Pacific Elementary School officials said students were safe and sheltering in place, and staff had seen only rain. KSBW
